function.name: get_all_devices
function.description: List all DLU devices/stations for a group. Returns dlu_id and dlu_config_id needed for data calls. Use grpId=-1 for all groups, detail: 0=properties only, 1=with channels and data, 2=with config, 3=with forecast. Supports output formatting as JSON (default) or flattened CSV, and output as text (default) or downloadable file.

grpId.description: Group ID filter (-1 for all groups)

filter.description: Optional semantic filter. Examples: 'offline', 'not offline', 'type is wsca or wsc agrar', 'online and name contains Göttingen', 'temperatur between 5 and 10', 'name like Berlin', 'name not contains Test', 'name starts with AWS', 'name ends with Nord'

fields.description: Optional comma-separated field selection with semantic matching. Supports top-level fields and channel selectors. Use 'channel.temperature' style, or plain unknown terms like 'temperatur'/'airpressure' to search channels by cha_name_en/cha_name_ger. Multiple channel terms use AND condition. Examples: 'name,type,channels', 'name,instant_data updated', 'name,id,channel.temperature,channel.humidity', 'name,id,temperatur,airpressure'.

format.description: Output format: json (default), csv (flattened), or excel (flattened as .xlsx).

output.description: Output mode: text (default) or file (base64 payload).

language.description: Language for channel labels used in CSV column naming.

function.name: get_devices_by_name
function.description: Search for specific DLU stations by name or partial string (e.g., "Berlin"). Canonical name-search tool for stations/devices. Supports wildcard '*' (internally converted to '%') and comma-separated name lists (e.g., "Lengden, Göttingen"). Supports semantic filter/fields projection and text/file output shaping. Returns device info including IDs and available sensor channel names.

dluName.description: DLU name/custom name query. Supports '*' wildcard and comma-separated list (each query is executed and appended), e.g. 'Lengden, Göttingen' or 'DLU*T, Göttingen'.

grpId.description: Group ID filter (-1 for all groups)

filter.description: Optional semantic filter. Examples: 'offline', 'not offline', 'type is wsca or wsc agrar', 'online and name contains Göttingen', 'temperatur between 5 and 10', 'name like Berlin', 'name not contains Test', 'name starts with AWS', 'name ends with Nord'

fields.description: Optional comma-separated field selection with semantic matching. Supports top-level fields and channel selectors. Use 'channel.temperature' style, or plain unknown terms like 'temperatur'/'airpressure' to search channels by cha_name_en/cha_name_ger. Multiple channel terms use AND condition. Examples: 'name,type,channels', 'name,instant_data updated', 'name,id,channel.temperature,channel.humidity', 'name,id,temperatur,airpressure'.

format.description: Output format: json (default), csv (flattened), or excel (flattened as .xlsx).

output.description: Output mode: text (default) or file (base64 payload).

language.description: Language for channel labels used in CSV column naming.

filter.description: Optional semantic filter applied to the resolved device (supports contains/has/like/not contains/starts with/ends with and numeric comparisons like between, >, <).

Examples: 'name,type,channels', 'name,instant_data updated', 'name,id,channel.temperature,channel.humidity', 'name,id,temperatur,airpressure'.

function.name: get_json_measurement_data
function.description: ALTERNATIVE: Fetch sensor measurements as JSON array. Use this ONLY when JSON structure is specifically needed for complex data processing. For general data retrieval, prefer get_csv_measurement_data. Supports both text output (default) and downloadable file format. Returns avg_data (always), min_data (optional), max_data (optional). When output_type="file": if only avg_data exists, creates single JSON file; if min/max data exists, creates ZIP file with separate _avg.json, _min.json, _max.json files. Use "hour" for relative time or "fromDate/toDate" (YYYYMMDDHHmmss) for fixed ranges. Use maxRows to limit the number of returned rows. Use fromLast=true to get rows from the end (e.g. maxRows=1 + fromLast=true returns only the latest measurement row).

dluId.description: DLU Device ID or array of IDs (required when filter is not provided)

dlu_id.description: Alias for dluId. DLU Device ID, comma-separated ID list (e.g. "101,102,103"), or array of IDs (required when filter is not provided)

grpId.description: Group ID for filter-based station selection (-1 for all groups)

detail.description: Detail level for filter-based station selection

filter.description: Optional semantic filter for station selection (recommended). Examples: 'offline', 'station type is dlu', 'temperatur > 10', 'name contains Göttingen'.

hour.description: Hours back from now. Defaults to 1 when hour, fromDate, and toDate are all missing.

channels.description: Channel selection: "ALL", "[ALL]", "*", or "[]" for all channels; or comma-separated mix of indices and semantic names like "1,24,air temperature,global strahlung". Unknown names are ignored.

fileName.description: Optional filename (without extension) when output_type is "file"

output_type.description: Output format: "text" for direct data (default), "file" for downloadable JSON file

maxRows.description: Optional row limit (0 or null = all rows). Use with fromLast=true to retrieve e.g. only the last measurement record.

fromLast.description: If true, take rows from the end (tail) of the dataset instead of from the top. Use maxRows=1 + fromLast=true to get only the latest measurement row.

function.name: get_csv_measurement_data
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL: Fetch sensor measurement data as CSV format. This is the default and recommended tool for retrieving sensor readings, temperature data, weather data, or any measurement values. Supports both text output (default) and downloadable CSV file format. Returns avg_data (always), min_data (optional), max_data (optional). When output_type="file": if only avg_data exists, creates single CSV file; if min/max data exists, creates ZIP file with separate _avg.csv, _min.csv, _max.csv files. Use "hour" parameter for relative time (e.g., last 6 hours) or "fromDate/toDate" (YYYYMMDDHHmmss) for specific date ranges. Use maxRows to limit the number of returned rows. Use fromLast=true to get rows from the end (e.g. maxRows=1 + fromLast=true returns only the latest measurement row).

dlu_id.description: Alias for dluId. DLU Device ID, comma-separated ID list (e.g. "101,102,103"), or array of IDs (required when filter is not provided)

detail.description: Detail level for filter-based station selection

filter.description: Optional semantic filter for station selection (recommended). Examples: 'offline', 'station type is dlu', 'temperatur > 10', 'name contains Göttingen'.

hour.description: Hours back from now. Defaults to 1 when hour, fromDate, and toDate are all missing.

fileName.description: Optional filename (without extension) when output_type is "file"

output_type.description: Output format: "text" for direct data (default), "file" for downloadable CSV file

function.name: get_excel_measurement_data
function.description: Export sensor measurement data as Excel (.xlsx) file with multi-sheet support. Creates separate sheets for average, minimum, and maximum values when available. Use this when users specifically request Excel format or need data for spreadsheet analysis. Returns avg_data sheet (always), min_data sheet (if available), max_data sheet (if available). Use "hour" parameter for relative time (e.g., last 24 hours) or "fromDate/toDate" (YYYYMMDDHHmmss) for specific date ranges. Use maxRows to limit the number of returned rows. Use fromLast=true to get rows from the end (e.g. maxRows=1 + fromLast=true returns only the latest measurement row).

dluId.description: DLU Device ID or array of IDs (required when filter is not provided)

dlu_id.description: Alias for dluId. DLU Device ID, comma-separated ID list (e.g. "101,102,103"), or array of IDs (required when filter is not provided)

grpId.description: Group ID for filter-based station selection (-1 for all groups)

detail.description: Detail level for filter-based station selection

filter.description: Optional semantic filter for station selection (recommended). Examples: 'offline', 'station type is dlu', 'temperatur > 10', 'name contains Göttingen'.

hour.description: Hours back from now. Defaults to 1 when hour, fromDate, and toDate are all missing.

channels.description: Channel selection: "ALL", "[ALL]", "*", or "[]" for all channels; or comma-separated mix of indices and semantic names like "1,24,air temperature,global strahlung". Unknown names are ignored.

addMinMax.description: Set to 1 to include min/max data sheets (optional)

maxRows.description: Optional row limit (0 or null = all rows). Use with fromLast=true to retrieve e.g. only the last measurement record.

fromLast.description: If true, take rows from the end (tail) of the dataset instead of from the top. Use maxRows=1 + fromLast=true to get only the latest measurement row.

function.name: get_measurement_data_in_chart
function.description: Fetch sensor measurement data and automatically generate a chart/plot. Supports line charts (time series), bar charts (categorical), scatter plots (correlation), and statistical summary (histogram, box plot, Q-Q plot, sequential). Use this when users request data visualization or charts. Output modes: png (default image), pdf (simple table-first report), excel (data sheet + chart sheet). If the user asks for a line chart of the last N hours, call this tool with chart_type: 'line' and hour: N. Same parameters as get_csv_measurement_data plus chart_type/output. Use maxRows to limit the number of data points in the chart. Use fromLast=true to chart the most recent N points.

hour.description: Hours back from now. Defaults to 1 when hour, fromDate, and toDate are all missing.

channels.description: Channel selection: "ALL", "[ALL]", "*", or "[]" for all channels; or comma-separated mix of indices and semantic names like "1,24,air temperature,global strahlung". Unknown names are ignored.

chart_type.description: Chart type: "line" for time series, "bar" for categorical comparison, "scatter" for correlation, "statistics" for 4-panel statistical summary (histogram, box plot, Q-Q plot, sequential)

output.description: Output format: png image (default), pdf report (table + chart), or excel workbook (table + chart sheet).

addMinMax.description: Set to 1 to include min/max datasets in chart (optional)

maxRows.description: Optional row limit (0 or null = all data points). Use with fromLast=true to chart the most recent N points.

fromLast.description: If true, take rows from the end (tail) of the dataset. Use with maxRows to chart the most recent N points.

function.name: get_channel_names
function.description: Retrieve specific sensor labels and indices for DLU devices. Useful for mapping user queries (e.g., "Air Temp") to correct channel numbers.

function.name: get_server_datetime
function.description: Get current server date and time. Required for queries with relative dates like yesterday, tomorrow, last week, last Monday, since Tuesday, or any date calculations. Returns current server timestamp to calculate historical date ranges.

function.name: get_server_timestamp
function.description: Required for time calculations, date conversions, and when working with timestamps. Use alongside get_server_datetime for relative date queries like yesterday, last week, or historical data ranges

function.name: generate_interactive_map_html
function.description: Generate an interactive HTML map with labeled station markers using Folium. Supports station filtering (recommended) via semantic filter expressions, works offline, supports zoom/pan, and includes enriched popup information for each device.

grpId.description: Group ID filter for auto-loading devices (-1 for all groups)

detail.description: Detail level for auto-loading devices. Use 1 to include channels/current data.

filter.description: Optional semantic filter for station selection (recommended). Examples: 'offline', 'station type is dlu', 'temperatur > 10', 'name contains Göttingen'.

markers.description: Array of device locations with coordinates and names

fileName.description: Custom filename for the generated map (without extension)

function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Get weather forecast data (Apple WeatherKit). Returns alerts and hourly meteorological metrics as JSON, PDF report, or Excel workbook based on output mode. Supports limiting forecast horizon via hours.

hours.description: Number of forecast hours to include from forecastHourly.hours.

output.description: Output format: text (JSON object), pdf (report as file), or excel (xlsx with data + chart images).

title.description: Optional report title for PDF/Excel output. Defaults to 'Weather forecast'.
